reviews.title: Bugs Galore, Not That Great
reviews.text:
Not the app I hoped it would be. While the sheep debit number is a bit useful and the guidance section taught me it reminded me of a free things, the app is so full of bugs it’s ridiculous. 

For example there is a two hour difference between the “morning peak” the Home tab and the Energy tab tell me. With an I supposed to believe?

Additionally I switched most of my notifications to “text” instead of app notifications, which seems like a great and unique system if you hate  notifications like me, but bugs galore again, I’m still getting notifications IN ADDITION to the text messages, so there’s no way to stop them, I already set the settings to how I wanted them!

Also they have a complicated and annoying system if you want to fill out a bug report.

Finally I had hoped it would actually *actively coach* you and set a day by day schedule for you to slowly shift your sleep to a more work-appropriate time, but no, app is recommending I go to be at 1AM to “match” my melatonin window. I don’t want to MATCH it you dinguses, I want to MOVE it!

Really feels like false advertising on that last one. Even without bugs I would be disappointed, it’s not just what they claimed to advertise in the App Store/setup phase.

I guess I’ll give it another week since there are a few things I like (such as the reminder to stop looking at screens/put on orange glasses), but I am planning to ask for the full-refund-within-your-first-month.

It’s not at all worth $70.

I have contacted RISE several times and provided evidence that I was still within the free trial period, along with proof that I had cancelled the subscription. Unfortunately, I have received no response and, so far, no refund has been issued.

I find this extremely disappointing and frustrating. I cancelled within the trial period and should not have been charged £22.99. I would strongly recommend being very careful when signing up for the free trial and checking your bank account to make sure you are not charged unexpectedly.

reviews.title: More or less broken compared to earlier iterations
reviews.text:
I used it in the past with no problem. Now it only works about 30% of the time and I’m being generous. It constantly changes sleep debt and energy, seemingly without any particular reason going from 84% of 5% even though nothing changed. But that’s not the worst part. The worst part is that it logs sleep when I’m clearly up and moving around which both my phone and my watch would indicate and it’s even before the recommended sleep window, and then when I actually do sleep, it doesn’t log it at all. It’s so inconsistent with this. It will work for one night and then just won’t work for three nights. Also particularly wonderful is how the smart alarm only goes off maybe three times out of 10. You literally could not trust it to wake you up.

I want to like it as much as when I used it a few years ago, but it has become so bloated and so confusing and getting itself tripped up with Apple health and the various different sleep schedules that exist between different devices, and you can spend hours trying to untangle it yourself and everything should be working and then it just doesn’t. 

It should also be worth noting the UI has become horrible. There is way too much going on and you cannot find basic useful things that you might use frequently.

reviews.text:
The app took the data from my phone and told me I should go to bed at my current average bed time and wake up at my average wake up time - not hugely insightful
If you don’t have a wearable it calculates your sleep based on when you touch your phone - again not very insightful
I also cancelled the subscription a day into the trial and it charged me anyway

reviews.title: Always feels like a scam
reviews.text:
I thought that I might come back to this, but honestly all the underhanded marketing makes it feel like a scam. I did the quiz on Instagram to find my ideal bedtime. Loads of questions, but at the end no ideal bedtime, just a link to install the app. I felt cheated. 

Then a day or so later on Instagram popped up an ad that was written as an apology, although it more looked like the next part of a cynical marketing campaign. They said as an apology they were giving away a week’s free access. 

I installed the app, but no free week. This is why I uninstalled it in the first place. Everything feels like a cynical and underhanded ploy to part people with their money. 

How can you trust what they claim!?

I was very excited to try this app as I’m 13 and has anxiety and really struggles with sleeping,but then I realized you had to  pay to use the app,and I don’t have money to pay for it so now I have to try find a free app that is probably not as good….

reviews.title: Leaves ghost alarms on your phone
reviews.text: I tried this app but decided it wasn’t for me - it didn’t get my sleep phases right, it marked periods when I was reading as deep sleep. So I cancelled the trial and removed the app. Now there is an alarm going off at an undesirable time every night that I can’t turn off, I’ve tried everything, including contacting Rise support. They first suggested turn off all haptics on my phone - but I don’t think this is acceptable as it means I can’t fully use my phone. Then they said they would escalate this matter to the team but it has been a couple weeks now, waking up by this alarm every night, and I have heard nothing back. I suppose the only thing left is a hard reset of the phone.

reviews.title: Privacy invasion AND payment? No.
reviews.text:
I really wanted to use this app, but I actually read privacy policies and you lost me at: 

'We may engage advertising partners, including third party advertising companies and social media companies, to display ads on the Service. These companies may use cookies and similar technologies to collect information about your interaction with the Service, our communications and other online services.'

In other words, people PAY you for the app and you still subject them to ADS and TRACKING across the Internet.

Yes, users 'can' opt out of tracking - IF willing and able to invest the time and energy required to establish the multi-faceted 12 point generic plan which must be manually replicated on every device. 

It's a paid app, so how about just not exploiting user's health data for additional profit in the first place? It's disgraceful.

reviews.title: A bit annoying
reviews.text: This app has problems knowing when I’m sleeping, I have my phone charging on a night stand but very often does not register my sleep. The main problem is the app then recalculates your sleep pattern which then put my sleep time a few hour later and wake when I should be at work. I have a routine and work and family obligations I don’t have to freedom to have to stay in bed. It would be good if it didn’t recalculate all the time.

reviews.title: borderline unusable w/o a subscription
reviews.text:
TLDR- to all the app developers out there: please!!! im begging! i’m on my hands and knees! get this in ur head: EVERYTHING DOES NOT HAVE TO BE A GODD*MN SUBSCRIPTION

ugh. upon download, u take a short sleep assessment and grant the app data from ur health app. it generates some general analysis, and then boom, dead end. a tab pops up to “start ur free trial” and u can’t even X out to read back over the advice they just gave you without first agreeing to subscribe. 
*to be clear!* i’m all in favor of paying app developers for their work! and while i hate ads, id be happy to pay a one-time purchase for a solid sleep tracker/management app- trust me, my sleep schedule is bad enough that it’d be worth it! but the subscription model is meant for services that continuously provide u new products/content, that’s why you keep paying. what they are NOT meant for: an app that’s basically just an upgrade to apple’s health app. 
imagine you buy a blender. now imagine the only way to get that blender to turn on is by sending monthly payments to the blender manufacturer. we would all agree that that’s ridiculous, right? this is a digital form of the exact same thing, but because it’s so commonplace on digital platforms, users are supposed to just accept this absurdity as the default monetization option? yeah, no. sorry, but i think i’ll pass

reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text: Charges u 99p per month apparently then try’s to take out £60  a month later don’t recommend

reviews.title: Does not work if you wake in the night
reviews.text: I have a toddler and occasionally wake at most once during the night to go and get him back to sleep. I am usually up 5-10 mins max. According to rise this means my sleep between 10-1 is nonexistent, and only my sleep between 1-7 counts for sleep tracking. So i am generally asleep for 8-9 hours but it consistently only tracks 5-6 hours. I have tried manually changing the sleep data but it will only let me go so far, not into the previous day. Unfortunately this is making the app unusable for me. I just cant believe such a basic feature is not supported. What if I needed the toilet in the night and used my phone as a torch? Seems a shame as the app is otherwise great.

reviews.title: Can’t account for waking up for work…
reviews.text:
I saw so many ads for Rise on Instagram that I finally tried it. I don’t understand how they think it could be useful for the average person because there is no way to indicate if you have a firm wake-up time because you have to get up for work. My app continually told me to go to bed *later* and get up later (after the time I already have to be at work). I communicated with their customer service and they said “At the moment, the app isn’t able to fully account for fixed wake times or situations where your schedule can’t be shifted—it’s designed to give guidance based on ideal sleep windows, so unfortunately it can’t adjust your recommendations around every individual constraint.” 

So….I guess download this app if you live a life of luxury and don’t ever have to get up at a fixed time? Hope this is helpful for the landed gentry of the 1800s!

UPDATE: They responded to this review asking me to contact their support team so they can help me, but I have already been in touch with the support team. I’m not having an “issue” with the app- I’m just pointing out that this app only works if you have literally no obligations to get up in the morning for. I’m honestly confused as to why so many people love it.

reviews.title: False metrics
reviews.text: I wear an Oura ring and an Apple Watch at night and also track with the Rise app … for 6 months now. This app is bogus IF you compare it with other tracking devices. It works if you have nothing else TO FOCUS YOUR ATTENTION on your sleep/rest hygiene. I suffered from severe insomnia for 2 years after a number of surgeries. I started to actively deal with this problem and have finally gone from almost 20 hours of sleep debt to 0! But Rise still tells me I have multiple hours of debt when I’ve been sleeping 7-8 hours every night with several up to 9 hours for the past 2 months. Utterly bogus. If you are really serious about your health and sleep, and can afford it of course, fork out the money for an OURA ring.  My Apple Watch (not a necessary device for this) and my Oura ring track nearly simultaneously. Rise metrics are never in line with these other 2 devices. What’s wrong with this picture??? The layout of the Rise App is pretty and flashy … but IMO useless. And the other metrics that I get from my ring have really helped me dial in better health. When my Oura ring suddenly alerted me that my body was under severe strain … I listened and went to bed for 2 days straight. In another period I would have ignored it and powered on. I keep a close eye on my HRV and am learning what raises it and what lowers it. So I am NOT a fan of Rise AFTER 6 MONTHS of continuous use.
